A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PII-Bench and retain matching core tasks, datasets, and experiments. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original human evaluations and model experiments, including Tables 2 and 4-7 and the additional PII-multi results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds privacy-utility experiments, smaller-model evaluations, and results on the new PII-Real dataset.

M1.justification: The published construction prompts receive limited procedural refinements: Figures 10-11 add explicit conflict checks and relationship constraints, including a parent-child age gap of at least 18 years. The core masking strategy and detection prompts remain unchanged; regeneration of the existing benchmark is not established.

E1.justification: v2 adds PII-Real: 100 instances derived from 20 actual AI researchers' public profiles, with expert-written queries and manual annotations. This extends evaluation beyond synthetic profiles and generated queries to authentic biographical information; the original synthetic coverage remains.

E2.justification: Tables 11-13 add Qwen2.5-0.5B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, and Qwen2.5-3B as evaluated baselines across the three tasks. This extends the existing Qwen model family while retaining the earlier main model and prompting comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.5 and Appendix F.2 introduce a 200-description response-evaluation protocol using three masking conditions, GPT4o generation, BGE-M3 similarity, Claude-3.7-Sonnet judging, randomized response order, and equal privacy-utility weighting. Section 3.3 also corrects the stated sample counts from 2,000 each to 1,214 and 1,228, matching the existing Table 3 rather than establishing resampling.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative privacy-utility analysis, synthetic-versus-real consistency analysis, and an investigation of deployment feasibility using smaller models. It removes v1's Figure 5 and associated PII-type performance analysis, while retaining the original complexity and challenging-set analyses.

E5.justification: Table 14 adds Spearman correlation tests with reported p-values below 0.001. Table 21 newly reports Fleiss' kappa values of 0.912 and 0.873 alongside the retained observed agreement rates. Existing human uncertainty reporting remains; additional experimental runs or seeds are not documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for smaller models and PII-Real, plus Table 8's privacy, utility, and balanced scores of 0.83, 0.89, and 0.86 for query-unrelated masking. The original core benchmark tables and PII-multi results retain their values. The per-type accuracy results in v1's Figure 5 are removed.

T1.justification: The original task definitions and Equations 1-16 are retained. Appendix F adds formal definitions for privacy protection, utility evaluation, weighted privacy-utility balance, and Performance Consistency Score in Equations 17-21. These extend the scoring framework without adding theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2's conclusion drops the numerical headline bounds F1 greater than 0.90 and F1 below 0.63, expressing the detection-versus-relevance gap qualitatively. The proposed masking strategy, benchmark contribution, and novelty claims remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 interprets synthetic-real agreement as evidence of real-world validity, smaller-model failures as a barrier to on-device protection, and the new tradeoff scores as supporting selective masking. It removes the earlier PII-type mechanism explanation. The dedicated limitations section remains essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendices C-D substantially document consistency optimization, relationship constraints, scenario generation, and filtering. v2 also adds a scenario-generation template, detailed annotation guidelines, PII-Real sourcing information, the utility-judge prompt and model identities, and disclosure of top_k=1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Chen et al. (2017) and M3-embedding (2024), supporting the BiLSTM-CRF discussion and embedding metric respectively. The related-work discussion and positioning of query-aware privacy protection are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v2 condenses construction, human-evaluation, and results prose; clarifies seven PII types versus 55 subcategories; and corrects terminology and wording. New subsections and expanded appendices organize the additions, while the main narrative sequence and substantial portions of the text remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds extensive displays for tradeoffs, smaller models, real-data results, consistency statistics, and annotation guidance. It redraws Figure 1, removes the per-type accuracy plot, adds a real-profile example and two prompt figures, and relocates appendix tables and interface screenshots.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important evidence gaps in v1 by adding quantitative response-utility evaluation and validation beyond synthetic data. Together with smaller-model experiments and substantially clearer construction documentation, these additions strengthen the paper's empirical support and reproducibility. The gains outweigh the lost per-type analysis, although PII-Real covers a narrow researcher population and the combination of the two utility measures remains unspecified.
